title: Forcible Sale of Nanking Government Flags

page_data.en:
Misc. 336/41
Pootoo Road
29th December, 41

1

Forcible sale of Nanking Government flags
in Pootoo Road District.
----------

At 11 a.m. 29/12/41, C.D.C. 145 received a telephone
call from one of the residents of Yue Ching Li, Robison
Road, to the effect that a male Japanese accompanied by
four male Chinese were forcibly selling Nanking Govern-
ment flags.

F.P.S. 702 Kono accompanied by C.D.C. 145 attended
and brought to this station the following persons:-
K. Sato (佐藤), 18, Japanese, and two male
Chinese, (1) Chang Ah Foh (姜河光) and (2) Yang Yoong
Ling (楊永林), employees of the Oriental Restoration
National Flag Co. (復興东亚國旗公司), 440/11 Canton Road.

Enquiries revealed that the aforementioned persons
had sold a number of flags at $6.00 each and 14 purchasers
had came together with the arrested persons to this
station to complain against having been forced to
purchase the flags.

The Japanese Gendarmerie were informed through the
Japanese Office, they attended this station and took the
three men to the Gordon Road Gendarmerie Headquarters.

The Gendarmerie officials refunded the money to the
14 purchasers, and cautioned the three arrested persons
afterwhich they released them.

Special Branch informed.

普陀路
1941年12月29日

1

普陀路地区强行出售南京政府旗帜案。
---

1941年12月29日上午11时，第145号中国籍巡长（C.D.C. 145）接到罗别根路（Robison Road）越庆里一名居民的电话，称一名日本男子 accompanied by 四名中国男子正在强行出售南京政府旗帜。

第702号外籍巡捕（F.P.S.）小野（Kono）在第145号中国籍巡长的陪同下前往现场，并将下列人员带至本警署：-
佐藤（K. Sato），18岁，日本人，以及两名中国男子，(1) 姜河光（Chang Ah Foh）和 (2) 楊永林（Yang Yoong Ling），系广东路440/11号“复兴东亚国旗公司”（Oriental Restoration National Flag Co.）的雇员。

经查询查明，上述人员以每面6.00元的价格出售了若干旗帜，14名购买者随被捕人员一同来到本警署，投诉其被迫购买旗帜。

已通过日本办事处通知日本宪兵队，他们抵达本警署，并将这三名男子带往戈登路宪兵队总部。

宪兵队官员向14名购买者退还了钱款，并对三名被捕人员进行了训诫，随后将其释放。

已通知特务处（Special Branch）。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.

REPORT

S. 1, Special Branch XXXXXX Station: File No.................... Date December 22, 1941.

SUBJECT: Forcible sale of flags and
calendars in the Settlement.

For the past few days, groups of four
or five persons each including one or two Formosans
visited various shops and residneces in the
Settlement, forcing the inmates to purchase
quantities of badges of Wang Ching-wei, President
of the Nanking Government, and Chinese National
Flags according to the number of inmates. The
badges are priced at $0.50 each and the flags at
$6.00 or $8.00 each. They threaten to report
to the Japanese authorities and have those who
fail to purchase arrested.

It is also reported that people claiming
to belong to an "East Asia Society" (東亞社)
sponsored by the Propaganda Department of the
Administrative Yuan of the Nanking Government
are also paying house-to-house visits to various
residences in the Settlement. They offer for
sale calendars at $1.80 each. They threaten the
residents that should they fail to purchase,
reports will be made to the authorities and drastic
action taken against them.

Elo 22/12.）

A.C. (Special Branch)

Kao Yen-kun

上海公共租界工部局警务处。

报告

特务处 XXXXXX 分署：档案号 ____ 日期 1941年12月22日。

主题：租界内强行出售旗帜及日历。

过去几天，每组四至五人（其中包括一至两名台湾人）的团伙走访租界内的各家商铺和住宅，强迫住户根据居住人数购买一定数量的汪精卫（南京政府主席）徽章和中国国旗。徽章定价为每枚0.50元，旗帜定价为每面6.00元或8.00元。他们威胁称，若不购买，将向日本当局举报并逮捕相关人员。

另据报道，自称隶属于南京政府行政院宣传部赞助的“东亚社”（東亞社）的人员，也在逐户走访租界内的各住宅。他们以每本1.80元的价格出售日历。他们威胁居民，若不购买，将向当局举报并采取严厉措施。

Bubbling Well.
Misc.No.578/41.
21st, Dec, 1941.

Arrest of two male Chinese whilst forcing
the sale of Nanking Government flags.

SIR,

At 11 a.m. on the 21-12-41, C.P.C. 2953 brought to
the station two male Chinese named :-

(1). Ngai Tao Wa (倪者和), 19, s/vegetable
hawker, a native of Koupo, residing in
room but off Connaught Road, O.O.L. and

(2). Ngai Lung Wa (倪文和), 25, S/Vegetable
hawker, a native of Koupo, same address.

who were arrested in Lane 1258 Avenue Foch at
10.50 a.m. this inst., whilst forcing the sale of
Wang Ching Wei flags.

On enquiries being made by C.D.C. 165 and D.C.I.
Possington, it was ascertained that the two accused
had been issued with 50 flags by one Tseu Hung Ping
(周鴻賓), a vegetable hawker occupying room 48 of
the Yoong Loh (長樂旅社) lodging house, No.440/11
Canton Road with instructions to sell same in the
aforementioned Lane, at $6.00 each.

The D.O."B" Div. and D.D.O."B" Div. on being made
acquainted with the facts of the case, gave instruct-
ions for the two accused, together with six remaining
flags, to be handed over to the Japanese Gendarmerie
Headquarters, No. 1288 Bubbling Well Road. These in-
structions were duly carried out through D.S. 777 T.
Furukawa.

Details re:- Tseu Hung Ping communicated to Louza
Station with request for action by that station.

CMH.
J. Possington
D. S. I.

静安寺。
杂项编号 578/41。
1941年12月21日。

两名中国男子在强行出售南京政府旗帜时被捕。

先生，

1941年12月21日上午11时，第2953号中国籍巡捕（C.P.C.）将两名中国男子带至警署，姓名如下：-

(1). 倪者和（Ngai Tao Wa），19岁，职业/菜贩，高邮人，住康纳路（Connaught Road）O.O.L. 某房间，及

(2). 倪文和（Ngai Lung Wa），25岁，职业/菜贩，高邮人，住址同上。

二人于当日上午10时50分在霞飞路（Avenue Foch）1258弄被捕，当时他们正在强行出售汪精卫旗帜。

经第165号中国籍巡长（C.D.C.）和波辛顿（Possington）副督察长（D.C.I.）查询，查明两名被告是由周鴻賓（Tseu Hung Ping）发给50面旗帜的。周鴻賓是一名菜贩，居住在广东路440/11号长乐旅社（Yoong Loh lodging house）48号房间，他指示二人在上述弄堂内以每面6.00元的价格出售这些旗帜。

B区警务总监和B区副警务总监在获悉案情后，指示将两名被告连同剩余的六面旗帜一并移交给位于静安寺路1288号的日本宪兵队总部。该指示已由第777号外籍巡捕（D.S.）古川（T. Furukawa） duly 执行。

关于周鴻賓的详细情况已通报卢家嘴警署，请该警署采取行动。

CMH.
J. Possington
副督察长

Jan. 7, 41.

Attempt to Force Sale of Nanking Regime Flags.
// and D.S.I. Elders.

Sir,

At 1.45 p.m. 6-1-42 the undermentioned two persons came to Chengtu Road Station after having quarrelled at the home of the 2nd named:-

1. Wong Bei Ching (王培金), 47, Anhwei, M/coolie, 4 Honan Road.
2. Kung Tuh Lo (公度羅), M/coolie, Lane 5/39 Chinhai Road.

Case was dealt with by the Charge-Room officer. The 2nd named stated that the 1st named had requested him to purchase a Nanking Regime flag and when he declined to do so the 1st named threatened to have him arrested by the Japanese Authorities.

The 1st named was warned against using any threats or force in selling such flags and both men were allowed to go.

I am, Sir,
Yours obediently,
T. Elders.
D. S. I.

D. D. O. "A"

Attempted forced sale of Nanking Government flags.

D.S. 61 u/r. S. Tooda Officer i/c.

Sir,
At 4.15 p.m. and 4.30 p.m. on 30-12-41, a male
Chinese named Lung K h Dih (孫國賢), residing 17 Sung
Liang Li, brought Pad and a female named Zung Yuin Sz

station and reported that between 4 p.m. and 4.15 p.m.

the sale of Nanking Government flags at $3.00 each.
According to the complainants these men had informed
them that failing a purchase being made they, complainants,
would possibly be subjected to "some trouble" in a few
days.
No purchase was made by either complainant Both
were informed to notify the nearest Policemen if these
flag sellers returned.

December 23, 41.

Attempted forced sale of Nanking Government flags.

D.S. 775 Inouye. [Signature] officer i/c.

Sir,

I beg to report that at 1.20 p.m. on 23/12/41, one male Chinese named Lieu Ts Hwa ( 刘子华 ), 41, Shantung, P/Watchman, employed by the Central Bank of China, living at 382/39 Haiphong Road, brought to the station the following two male Chinese namely:-

(1) Pan Foh Kwei ( 潘馥奎 ), 23, Wusih, S/Unemployed, 440/11 Canton Road.
(2) Hwei Siang Dong ( 韓湘桐 ), 24, Wusih, S/Unemployed, 440/11 Canton Road.

From enquiries made by C.D.C. 331 and the undersigned ascertained the following facts:-

At about 1 p.m. even date, above mentioned two male Chinese approached the complainant's house and requested him to buy a Nanking Government flag for the sum of $6.00, however the complainant refused to purchase the flag owing to the fact that he had no money with him.

The above said two men, then, left the premises, but the complainant requested them to proceed to Gordon Road Station to report the matter.

The Japanese Gendarmerie were communicated with and they requested that the parties concerned be handed over to them. Handed over accordingly at 4 p.m. 23/12/41. D.O. "B" informed.

At 4.30 p.m. same date, F.S. 244, C.P.C.s 3055 and 2326 brought to the station the following named complainant and four accused:-

当日约下午3时，第一和第二被告前往报案人住所，要求其以6.00元的价格购买一面南京政府旗帜。

报案人拒绝购买，称其已于1941年12月22日购买过一面。第一和第二被告试图强行出售旗帜，因此，报案人以6.00元的价格购买了一面旗帜。

第一和第二被告离开现场，前往马克姆路（Markham Road）184号的茶馆，报案人跟随他们，并要求被告退款，因为他已于1941年12月22日购买过旗帜。

两被告拒绝，并打电话给位于福州路与四川路路口中興（Chung Shing）大楼24室的卖旗办事处。

约20分钟后，第三和第四被告来到现场，就上述旗帜的交易与报案人发生争执，此时隶属于普陀路警署的第124号中国籍巡长（C.D.C.）到达现场，建议所有人前往戈登路警署，第244号外籍巡捕（F.S.）、第3055号和2326号中国籍巡捕（C.P.C.s）

Sir,
At 11.35 p.m. on 21/12/41, Dr. Tsou Tang Tau (曹芳涛),
629/8 Seymour Road telephoned this station reporting that two
male Chinese were present at his home attempting to sell Nanking
Government flags at $6.00 each.

P.S. Kruse, **〔此处转录不清〕** 737 attended and found a
male Chinese named Li Ta Tong Liang (朱军良), 25, Ningpo,
Single, 14 Sung **〔此处转录不清〕** Road and a Japanese named
H. Yamayoshi, 30, residing 15 Sang Ching Lee off Tiendong Road,
attempting to sell these flags, 12 of which were then in their
possession.

Inquiries by S.I. Kimura, C.D.S. 173 and the undersigned
revealed that the Japanese was acting as an advisor and that
the Chinese was employed by the Tung Ya Lai Hwo (東亞聯合)
Company, 14 Zung Foh Li, Yoosung Road, Chapel to sell these
flags.

According to Dr. Tsau, the Chinese asked him to purchase
a flag failing which two "Shoong Dee" would visit his home on
22/12/41.

At 2 p.m. on 21/12/41, one Tseu Oong Ping (周鸿庆), 30,
Shanghai, manager of the above named factory came to this
station to intervene on behalf of the flag sellers. He also
was detained.

S.I. Kimura communicated with the Japanese Gendarmerie and
on their arrival it was learned that these flags were being sold
without their permission.

The Gendarmerie requested custody of these three men and
the twelve flags which was complied with on instructions from
D.O. "B".
Receipt attached.

美国 161 Muir. Eriooda 警官 主管。

先生，
1941年12月21日晚上11时35分，西摩路629/8号的曹芳涛博士致电本警署报告称，有两名中国男子在其家中试图以每面6.00美元的价格出售南京政府旗帜。

巡佐 Kruse，**〔此处转录不清〕** 737号 出警后发现一名名为朱军良（Li Ta Tong Liang）的中国男子，25岁，宁波人，单身，住嵩山路14号 **〔此处转录不清〕** ，以及一名名为 H. Yamayoshi 的日本男子，30岁，住天潼路桑庆里15号，正试图出售这些旗帜，当时他们手中持有12面旗帜。

经特别调查员 Kimura（C.D.S. 173）及本人查询，获悉该日本人是作为顾问行事，而该中国人受雇于耀生路查佩尔宗福里14号的东亚联合公司（Tung Ya Lai Hwo），负责销售这些旗帜。

据曹博士称，该中国人要求他购买一面旗帜，否则两名“兄弟”（Shoong Dee）将于1941年12月22日造访其家。

1941年12月21日下午2时，上述工厂经理周鸿庆（Tseu Oong Ping），30岁，上海人，来到本警署为卖旗者说情。他也被拘留。

特别调查员 Kimura 与日本宪兵队取得联系，待其到达后得知，这些旗帜是在未经他们许可的情况下出售的。

宪兵队要求接管这三名男子及十二面旗帜，根据“B”区副警务总监的指示，已照办。

On the morning of 29-12-41, a letter was received
at this station from the Eastern Asia Revival National
Flag Co., stating that this establishment had received
permission from the Japanese Special Service Corp.,
Shanghai to promote the sale of national flags, and
requesting that the Police allow the sale of such flags
in the International Settlement. A translation of the
letter is as follows:-

"Sir,
On the Dec. 8th, 1941, the Japanese Army and
Navy entered the International Settlement and
started to take responsibility for maintaining
peace and order.
In order to make the people in the Settlement
understand the "peace campaign" and the idea of
peace, we have obtained permission and a certifica-
te from the Japanese Special Service Organization
of Shanghai following an application being for-
warded to them, to promote the sale of "Peace and
Anti-Comintern" National Flags, so we have now sent
out flag-sellers to the Settlement to carry out
the sale of such flags. These sellers are each
in possession of a certificate issued by our
company (specimen enclosed).
We shall much appreciate if you render
us your assistance.
Our main office is located at 14 Zung Foh Li
off Foh Sung Road Chapel with a provisional Sales
Dept at 11/440 Canton Road (Tel:- 93948).

Tseu Hung Ping
(Representative)
29-12-41."

The letters and specimen certificate are attached
for favour of forwarding to Headquarters for disposal.
J.Y. Hillhouse
D. S. I.

1941年12月29日上午，本警署收到东亚复兴国旗公司来信，称该机构已获得日本上海特务机关的许可，推广销售国旗，并请求警方允许在国际租界内销售此类旗帜。信件译文如下：-

“先生，
1941年12月8日，日本陆海军进入国际租界，并开始承担维持和平与秩序的责任。
为了让租界民众理解‘和平运动’及和平理念，我们在向上海日本特务组织提出申请后，获得了许可及证书，以推广销售‘和平反共’国旗，因此我们现在已派遣卖旗者进入租界进行销售。这些销售人员每人持有一份由我公司颁发的证书（样本附后）。
如蒙协助，不胜感激。
我司总办事处位于福生路查佩尔宗福里14号，并在广东路11/440号设有临时销售部（电话：93948）。

周鸿平（代表）
1941年12月29日。”

At 12.30 p.m. 18/12/41 a telephone message was
received from S.I. Varndell (Louza) to the effect that
he had been called into the Beco Tailor Shop, 957
Bubbling Well Road where two male Chinese had attempted
to force the inmates to purchase a Nanking Regime flag
for $6.00. He had detained the two men and requested
that someone be sent to bring them to the station.

C.P.C.s 35 and 1724 attended and brought to the
station :-

(1) Zung Wong Kong (张鸿康), 24, Ningpo,
s/unemployed, 24 Wei San Li (维山里),
Pingliang Road

(2) Woo Sieu Kung (吴小公) 26, Zaushing,
s/unemployed, 49 Loong Zung Li (隆众里)
Pingliang Road

together with 24 flags and 24 receipts.

Enquiries by D.S.I. Taylor and C.D.C. 285 disclosed
that at 12.15 p.m. 18/12/41 the two above described
entered the Beco Tailor Shop, 957 B'Well Road and offered
to sell one of the flags for $6.00 to the proprietress
Mrs E. Braunschweiger, German Refugee. The latter refus-
ed same, but the two men were insistent and would not
leave the shop. The complainant then went out from the
shop and called S.I. Varndell, who happened to be passing
and letter informed the station.

进一步查询显示，这三名男子还于1927年10月14日上午9时（原文如此，疑为1941年之误）从一名叫女夷（Chui Yi）（音译）的女子那里购买了旗帜，该女子住大英酒店819室。随后他们将旗帜带到以下地址，共售出十八面旗帜——莫霍克路（Mohawk Road，即今海宁路或类似路段，暂按音译保留或依当时路名习惯，此处原文为Mohawk，通常对应海宁路Henan Rd? 不，Mohawk Rd是当时的海宁路旧称或附近小路，此处直译或保留）125、133、313、194、198、202、208和136号。以及威海卫路260、265、263、259、247、216、224、226和230号。

进一步查询显示，在上述售出的十八面旗帜中，只收到了十五面的付款，另外三面旗帜留在了上述三个地址，约定必须购买，款项稍后收取。出售的十五面旗帜的款项即90.00美元，连同一枚绿色金属徽章，编号41，上有以下铭文

中央执行委员会特许
复兴
党国旗界特派部

Louza
December 20, 1941.

NEW NATIONAL GOVERNMENT FLAG OFFERED FOR SALE

At 9.02 a.m. 19-12-41 a telephone message was
received at this Station from 25/20, Amoy Road report
ing that the above address had been visited by three
male Chinese who offered a flag for sale to the com-
plainant using a threatening attitude.

Upon receipt of this message, the undersigned
in company with D.S.Carr, C.D.C.136 proceeded to the
scene of occurrence where on the arrival it was learned
that three male Chinese had already left the complainants
house.

From enquiries it was revealed that the house is
a dwelling occupied by the complainant named Chiang
Zung Ching ( 〔此处转录不清〕 ), 25, Soochow, shop assistant in a
hardware shop and at about 9.50 a.m. even date he was
approached by three young male Chinese flag hawkers
(New National Government) and offered for sale, a flag
for $6.00.

Complainant stated that he refused to purchase
at first but later paid $6.00 after seeing that
the hawkers were intent on making trouble if he did
not make the purchase and fearing results of a political
nature.

D.D.O."A"Divn.

1941年12月20日。

出售新国民政府旗帜

1941年12月19日上午9时02分，本警局接到厦门路25/20号的电话留言，报告称上述地址有三名中国男子到访，以威胁态度向投诉人兜售旗帜。

收到此消息后，本人与卡爾（Carr）侦探长、华籍侦探主任第136号一同前往事发地点，到达时得知三名中国男子已离开投诉人家中。

经查询得知，该房屋为投诉人蒋宗庆（Chiang Zung Ching）（〔此处转录不清〕）居住的住宅，25岁，苏州人，五金店店员。同日约上午9时50分，三名年轻的中国男子（新国民政府）旗帜小贩接近他，并以6.00美元的价格向他兜售一面旗帜。

投诉人称，他起初拒绝购买，但后来看到小贩们执意制造麻烦，若不购买恐有政治性质的后果，于是支付了6.00美元。

Louza                                Dec. 30, 1941.

Forced Sale of Nanking Government Flag.

At 5 p.m. 30-12-41 J.D.S. 341 attached to C.I.
Crime Branch, Headquarters, brought to the station a
male Chinese named:-

Wei Ming (明), 38, Nanking, temporarily
residing, Room 29 Goong Lee (永芳) Lodging
House, Tientsin Road.

who he had arrested at his home, Lane 440/6 Tientsin
Road, in connection with forced sale a national peace
flag. From enquiries conducted by the undersigned the
following facts are ascertained that at about 4.30 p.m.
even date the above mentioned Chinese together with
three others and visited the C.D.S.'s address to sell
the Nanking Government's flag. The complainant refused
the proposal, owing to having bought a similar flag on
December 28th, however, meeting with the refusal, they
became in the threatening attitude, therefore the
complainant arrested Wei Ming, one of them while the
others made good their escape.

The Japanese Gendarmerie was informed and the
arrested man was handed over to Sergeant Nagata in
order to condemn his/their behaviour.

1941年12月18日上午10时40分，华捕第2684号将三名中国男子带至警局，即：
1. 许者兴（Hsu Tsai Shing），23岁，镇江人，单身/无业，住康纳路（Connaught Road）外庆寿庙（Ching S Too Miau）62号，老闸捕房辖区。

经刑事侦缉处第201号警探及本报告人查询得知，1941年12月18日上午10时30分左右，上述三人前往成都路565号一家名为“和顺”（Woo Sung）的米店，要求店员购买他们的一面旗帜。华捕第2684号目睹此情形后逮捕了这三人，因为他认为他们可能会制造麻烦并引发骚乱。侦探讯问了上述米店的店员，店员表示这三名男子并未试图强行推销其旗帜。

At 11.20 a.m. 30-9-41, C.P.C. 12 brought to the station two mal. Chinese (1) Wong Chi Yuen (錢佳賢), 21, Ningpo, s/unemployed, residing Nantao, and (2) Nih Vung : Yien (丰贤), 15, Ningpo, S/unemployed, residing Nantao, whom he had arrested at 11.10 a.m. 30-9-41 outside no.211 North Kiangse Road at the request of compt., Tien Tāh Yien (鐵法贤) who alleged that they and two others had attempted to persuade him to buy a Nanking Government flag for $5.00.

Inquiries ascertained that at 11.10 a.m.30-9-41 the above two described persons and two others named Nyi Ping Su (蘇炳水) and Yuan Zung Su (阮順水) not arrested, had visited compt's bicycle shop, 211 North Kiangse Road, and asked the compt. to purchase from them a flag at $5.00 per piece which the compt. refused and informed the C.P.C. who brought them to the station.

The compt. stated that they did not employ threats but insisted on him in purchasing the flags.

The arrested men stated that they are employed by one named Tse Ping (朱炳) who resides at No. 9 King Kong Leong alleyway, Rue Montauban, F.C. in the sale of flags in Shanghai.

D.D.O."C". informed and on his instructions the men were cautioned re appearing in this district again fo this purpose,and released.

1

在租界内出售中华民国国旗。

1941年9月30日上午11时20分，华捕第12号将两名中国男子带至警局：(1) 钱佳贤（Wong Chi Yuen），21岁，宁波人，单身/无业，住南市；(2) 丰贤（Nih Vung : Yien），15岁，宁波人，单身/无业，住南市。该员于1941年9月30日上午11时10分，应江西路（North Kiangse Road）211号店主铁法贤（Tien Tāh Yien）的要求，在江西路211号门外逮捕了上述二人。店主指控他们及另外两人曾试图劝说他以5.00元购买一面南京政府旗帜。

经查询得知，1941年9月30日上午11时10分，上述两名被描述的人员及另外两名未被逮捕的男子苏炳水（Nyi Ping Su）和阮顺水（Yuan Zung Su），曾光顾店主位于江西路211号的自行车店，并要求店主以每面5.00元的价格向他们购买旗帜，店主拒绝并通知了华捕，华捕遂将他们带至警局。

店主表示，他们并未使用威胁手段，但坚持要他购买旗帜。

被捕男子称，他们受雇于一名叫朱炳（Tse Ping）的人，此人住在法租界蒙托邦路（Rue Montauban）金刚弄（King Kong Leong alleyway）9号，在上海从事旗帜销售工作。

已通知“C”区副主管，并根据其指示，警告这些人不得再为此目的出现在本辖区，随后予以释放。

虹口警局三等巡官田中（Tanaka）725号来到本警局，讯问了被捕者，并查明他以每套3.50元的价格购得这些旗帜。他承认通过口头威胁强迫上述12人以每套5.00元购买，并称他这样做是因为目前失业且急需金钱。当被问及潜逃同伙的详细情况时，他表示不知道他们的姓名等，因为他仅在当天上午与他们相遇。

Date April 9 1940

Subject Flag Monopoly Bureau established at 75 Jessfield Road.

Made by. D.S.I. Liao Chung Chien. Forwarded by. D. I. Crawford.

A flag monopoly bureau under the name,
Foh Shing National and Party Flag Company (復興製銷党國旗公司),
has been established at No. 75 Jessfield Road, which
houses the various tangpu formed by the Wang Ching Wei
sponsored Kuomintang. It is in charge of the following
two persons:-
1. Waung Mei Yung (汪曼雲), an ex-committee member
of the local kuomintang Headquarters (defunct), who
joined the Wang Ching Wei party in 1939, and who has
since been made a member of the Central Executive
Committee of the Kuomintang sponsored by Wang.
2. Li Mong (李蒙), one of the secretaries of the
Special Service Corps of the Chung Kuo Kuomintang
Anti-Comintern and National Salvation Army, 76
Jessfield Road.

This new organ is in possession of a
certificate No. 192 issued by the new Central China
Government, Nanking, and will make endeavours to effect
control over the various flag manufacturing shops and
factories in Shanghai and other places occupied by
Japanese troops.

On April 7, 1940, a flag manufacturing
shop situated at No. 7, Yan Shing Li, off Brenan Road,
O. O. L., which is the only flag maker in the Jessfield
Area, was ordered to suspend business by the organ.

Liao Chung Chien.
D. S. I.

主题：在极司菲尔路75号设立的旗帜专卖局。

制作人：副督察长廖仲坚（Liao Chung Chien）。转呈人：督察 Crawford。

    一个名为“复兴制销党国旗公司”的旗帜专卖局已在极司菲尔路75号成立，该地址也是由汪精卫赞助的国民党各党部所在地。该局由以下两人负责：-
1. 汪曼雲（Waung Mei Yung），原本地国民党总部（已解散）执行委员，于1939年加入汪精卫派系，此后成为汪精卫赞助的国民党中央执行委员会委员。
2. 李蒙（Li Mong），极司菲尔路76号中国国民党反共救国军特别服务队秘书之一。

    这一新机构持有南京新华中政府颁发的第192号证书，并将努力控制上海及其他日军占领地区的各类旗帜制造商店和工厂。

    1940年4月7日，位于外摆渡路（O. O. L.）布伦安路旁严家弄7号的一家旗帜制造店（这是极司菲尔路地区唯一的旗帜制造商）被该机构责令停业。

During the past fortnight, it is reported, a
party of two Japanese and two Chinese (three wearing
foreign style clothing and the remaining one Chinese
long gown) visited various Chinese schools in the
Settlement and offered for sale maps of China purport-
ing to have been published by a Japanese in Changchun,
"Manchukuo" with the approval of the Japanese Military
Authorities. The names and addresses of the schools
known to have been visited are given hereunder:-

1. Dao Tsoong Girls Middle School (道中女中),
628 Avenue Road.
2. Au Kwong Middle School (夏光中学), 167 Tatung Road.
3. Shanghai Law College (上海法学院), 8 Wongkashaw Gar-
dens.
4. Zang Tsing Middle School (上青中学), 66 Tsingtao
Road.
5. Zung Woo Girls Middle School (人和女中), 3, Lane
310, Myburgh Road.
6. Kweng Van Girls Middle School (坤範女中), 331
Myburgh Road.
7. Lih Tuh Primary School (立德小学), 124 Park Road.
8. Kwang Ming Middle School (光明中学), 4, Lane 345,
Myburgh Road.
9. Kung Nyi Primary School (公義小学), Lane 741, No.
60, Chengtu Road.

The visitors strongly advised the school autho-
rities to buy the maps at $5.00 each on the ground that
the Sino-Japanese hostilities had changed the map of
China entirely and that the maps should be displayed
on the school premises in order to acquaint the students
of the actual situation. They insisted that as many

Sir:

At 11.30 a.m. 4/5/39 a telephone message was
received from 210/4 C.B. Road that a disturbance was
taking place at that address. S.S. Ith, P.C. 1066 Yen Tong
& C.D. 7 292 immediately proceeded to the scene and were
informed by Mr. Hu (胡叶贵), proprietor of I Han Tong (景董堂)
Medicine Shop, 312/4 Chekiang Road that a Japanese and two
Chinese had visited his shop and compelled him to purchase
for $1.00 a flag of the Reformed Government of China. He
stated that the persons were then in the shop next door
and therefore the Police party proceeded there and even-
tually brought all concerned to the station.

The Japanese is named: Tsubota and the two Chinese
: Lee Shing Lau (李安宝) age 38, native of Changchow, residing
room 20 Chi Loong Lodging House, Foochow Road and Hu Pao
Loong (吴宝荣) age 31, native of Tanyang, residing 7 Foo Yuen
Lee, Canton Road.

All three are attached to the Japanese Special Service
Mission.

From subsequent enquiries it was learned that at about
11.50 a.m. 4/5/39 the three persons went to the I Han Tong
Medicine Shop and demanded that the proprietor purchase a
flag from them. The proprietor stated that he did not want
one. He was then asked by the first named Chinese why he
did not want one and he replied that he had no money. He
was then asked by the same man with whom he had registered
his shop. On him replying that he had registered with the
Japanese authorities, he was told that he must buy a flag.
He repeated that he did not want one but was willing to
buy a Japanese flag if necessary. Then the spokesman
abused the complainant and seized him by the front of

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.

The following is the statement of Hu S Wei, the complainant.
native of Shingkiang taken by me A. A. 202.
at Chioxaiarr on the 4/5/39 translated by Clerk Ching
and interpreted by

Hu S Wei, age 37, native of Shingkiang, owner of the
I Yun Tong medicine shop, 342 Yulin Road, states as follows:-
"At about 11.45 a.m. 4/5/39 three men, two in foreign dress
and 1 in Chinese, came to my shop and offered for sale a five
barred flag. I told them that I did not want same. On hearing
this, the man in Chinese /dress/ asked me why I did not want
the flag and I replied that I had no money to buy same. The same
man then asked me with whom I had registered my shop. I replied
that I had registered with the Japanese Military Police Head-
quarters. He then told me that if I had registered with the
Japanese authorities, I should buy a five-barred flag. I then
said to him, "If you want me to buy a flag, I would prefer to
buy a Japanese flag." On hearing this the man was very angry
and abused me. He also seized me by the front of my long gown
and attempted to pull me out of the shop. At this juncture
the two men in foreign dress separated us from making further
trouble. At the same time one of my assistants named Dai
produced $1.00 and bought a five-barred flag from them. They
then left our shop and went to a neighbouring shop (barber shop).
After a short while, a party of Police (S.M.P.) came to the scene
brought me and the three men to Yulin Road Police Station. This
is my true statement."
(Signed, crossed and finger-printed) Hu S Wei.

胡S Wei，37岁，兴化（Shingkiang，音译）人，榆林路342号怡云堂（I Yun Tong）药店店主，陈述如下：
“1939年5月4日上午11时45分左右，三名男子，两人身着西装，一人身着中式服装，来到我的店铺兜售五色旗。我告诉他们我不需要。听到这话，那名穿中式服装的男子问我为什么不要这面旗帜，我回答说我没有钱购买。同一个人接着问我在哪里登记了店铺。我回答说我在日本宪兵司令部登记过。于是他告诉我，既然我在日本当局登记过，就应该买一面五色旗。我便对他说，‘如果你要我买旗帜，我宁愿买日本国旗。’听到这话，那人非常生气并辱骂我。他还抓住我长衫的前襟，试图把我拉出店铺。就在这时，那两名穿西装的男子将我们分开，以防止事态进一步恶化。同时，我的一名名叫戴（Dai）的店员拿出1.00美元从他们那里买了一面五色旗。随后他们离开我的店铺，去了隔壁的一家店铺（理发店）。过了一会儿，一队工部局警务处警察赶到现场，将我和那三名男子带到榆林路警署。这是我的真实陈述。”
（签名、画叉并按指印）胡S Wei。

Subject House 411, Markham Road - alleged to be residence of two employees of the Reformed Government employed in selling five bar flags in the Settlement (north of the Creek).

Made by D.S.I. Liao Chung Chien Forwarded by C Crawford. D.S.

FILE

7/5

（左侧手写批注：Lended to knowledge return 5/4 noted John Caly 5/5/39. deliver to Branch 6/5 R.F.）

In compliance with the instructions of D.C. (Special Branch) appended to the attached report (Wayside Misc. 170/39) on the subject of sale of five bar flags in the Settlement, discreet enquiries at house 411, Markham Road reveal that the chief tenant of the premises is the Hung Hong Wine Shop (宏康), 399-401 Markham Road. The ground floor is used as a godown by the wine shop while the rooms on the 1st floor (the house being a two-storeyed building) are sub-let to the following persons:-

| | Occupant |
| :--- | :--- |
| Front room: | Chen Chin Chia (陳金嘉), C.P.C. 680 attached to Sinza Station. |
| Back room: | Mrs. Soo (蘇), a widow, whose late husband formerly owned a tea shop in Chapei. |
| Room above kitchen: | Koo Ai Kwang (顧愛廣) Conductor 805 of the Shanghai Tramway Co. |

As none of the occupants answer to the names of Tsei Ts Ho (鄒子和) and Dau Zu-kung (陶汝根), the two employees of the Reformed Government employed in selling five bar flags in the Settlement (north of the Creek) mentioned in the attached report as residing at House 411, Markham Road, C.P.C. 680 was confidentially approached and enquired if any occupants of the house had relatives or friends bearing those names living with them. According to him, the other two occupants had no relatives or friends living with them but Mrs. Soo, the widow occupying the back room, was from time to time visited by her paramour named Tsei Tsing Foh

Sir,

At 1.00 p.m. on 28-4-39, a male Chinese named Wong Chin Ching (王金卿), employed as an assistant in a cloth shop at 1106 East Yuhang Road, came to the station and reported that two male Chinese who claimed to be members of the "Reformed Government" were selling "five bar" flags to all the shops on East Yuhang Road.

D. C. (Divs.)
Information: C.D.C.322 and the undersigned repaired to the scene where two male Chinese were observed carrying a number of "five bar" flags. They were interviewed and gave their names as Tsei Ts Ho (鄒子和), 52, Chinkiang, and Dau Zu Kung (陶汝根), 34, Quinsan, both residing 411 Markham Road. They produced passes issued by the "Reformed Government of Nanking" (維新政府) permitting them to sell "five bar" flags, which they were doing for $1.00 a piece, to all shop masters in that vicinity.

They were then asked if there were any stipulations or conditions connected with the purchase of these flags and they replied in the negative, saying that it was entirely voluntary whether the shop masters purchased a flag or not.

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
S. B. REGISTRY
The Significance of the National Flag No. S. B. D. 9111
Date ____ 5 3
Love your country, but love your
national flag first.

The National flag of a nation is a thing that represents
that nation and her national spirit. In view of the importance
attached to a national flag, it should be honoured by all citizens
who are loyal to their country.

The bright and brilliant flag of five colours, namely red,
yellow, blue, white and black, is at present flying in the new
republic of China. The Provisional Government at Peking and the
Reformed Government at Nanking, under this five-barred flag which
symbolizes unity, are leading the Chinese people to the task of
building a new republic of China for the glorification of the
ancient civilization and virtues of China.

In designing the five-barred flag, it was originally
intended to signify (1) internal harmony between the five Chinese
races, and (2) externally its peaceful existence with all nations
of the world. The high ideals manifested in the original creation
of this flag really deserve the respect of all Chinese citizens.

The five-barred flag now represents China and everything
that is Chinese at home and abroad. The people of the new China
can therefore best express their patriotism by hoisting the five-
barred flags. The "Monopoly Bureau for the sale of national flags"
has now been authorized by the Shanghai City Government as the
only official organ for the manufacture and sale of standard size
national flags and it is hoped that our people will realize the
importance of flying these flags which will serve to impress the
world of the bravery of the New China under the leadership of the
two new regimes.

FILE

（批：J.C.S.B.）

国旗的意义 编号 S. B. D. 9111
日期 ____ 5 3
爱国，但首先要爱国旗。

一个国家的国旗是代表该国及其民族精神的事物。鉴于国旗的重要性，所有忠于国家的公民都应尊重国旗。

目前，红、黄、蓝、白、黑五种颜色鲜艳明亮的旗帜正飘扬在新的中华民国上空。北京临时政府和南京维新政府在这面象征统一的五色旗领导下，正带领中国人民为建设新的中华民国而努力，以弘扬中国古代文明和美德。

在设计五色旗时，初衷是表示（1）中国五族内部的和谐，以及（2）对外与世界各国和平共处。这面旗帜最初创造时所体现的崇高理想，确实值得所有中国公民的尊重。

五色旗现在代表着中国以及海内外的一切中国事物。因此，新中国的人民可以通过悬挂五色旗来最好地表达他们的爱国情怀。“国旗专卖局”现已获得上海市政府授权，作为制造和销售标准尺寸国旗的唯一官方机构，希望我国人民认识到悬挂这些旗帜的重要性，这将向世界展示在两个新政权领导下新中国的英勇形象。

归档

（批：J.C.S.B.）
（批：J.B.）

Sir,

On the morning of the 28/4/39 a male Chinese
age about 20 years, height 5' 6", medium build, small
face, dark complexion, wearing dark brown long gown
and brown felt hat, speaking Norpo dialect, accompanied
by a male Japanese, age about 32 years, height 5' 7",
stout build, long face, wearing dark blue foreign
style suit and grey felt hat, visited the majority
of shops in Yangtzepoo district and forcibly sold
to a large number of shop-keepers at the rate of $1.00
each the Five Barred Chinese Flag under the threats
that if they refused to buy the flag they would be
arrested by the Japanese Military Authorities.

The shop-keepers who bought a flag were given
a pamphlet explaining the meaning of the flag and
directions how it should be flown, which, when
translated reads as follows:-

"The meaning of the National Flag."

"The National Flag is a sign representing its
country and the spirit of their people. Respecting our
country we must first pay our respect to our national
flag. The Five Barred flag is now flying all over
the new China. The Provisional Government at Peking
and the Reformed Government at Nanking under this flag
constitute the new China and people who love their
country must fly the flag to show their respect."

Instructions were given to the shop-keepers that
the flags must be flown on the 29/4/39 on the occasion

of the Reformed Government" was established in the

led by a Japanese carrying a number of five barred
flags and claiming to be officials of the "Shanghai

purchase at least one flag. Should a refusal be
met with, the occupants were informed that they would
be given three days in which to change their attitude,

Most of the shops fearing lest some action would be
taken against them accepted the flags.

RECORD OF INVESTIGATION.

Illegal functioning of a Member of The Police Bureau of The Shanghai City Government In Connection with The Sale of "Five Barred" Flags, In Kashing Road District.

（印：FILE）

Sir,

At 10.15 a.m. 28/3/1939, Sub Inspector Sharrock visited Kashing Road Station and reported that a member of the Police Bureau of the Shanghai City Government was entering premises on Suchow Road, and selling "Five Barred" flags to the residents.

Inspector Watson, J.P.S.S and the undersigned visited the scene, and found a male Chinese wearing the uniform of a inspector of the Police Bureau of the Shanghai City Government, accompanied by four male assistants in civilian dress, making a house-to-house visit along Suchow Road, and selling "Five Barred" flags to the householders.

Enquiries among residents ascertained the party demanded that the occupants of each house purchase a flag, at the price of $1.00 each, otherwise their number would be recorded and a report made to the Japanese Authorities, who would impose a fine of $6.00 cash.

When the purchase of a flag was made the person wearing uniform issued a printed receipt for the amount received.

RECORD OF INVESTIGATION.
Sale of Reformed Government Flags.
At 11.10 a.m. 27/3/39, D.I. Sharrock reported to Hongkew Station that he had observed a party of uniformed members of the City Government Police Bureau and civilian Chinese disposing of Reformed Government flags to residents on Century Road.
Investigations by D.C. 375 and D.S. Muir located a party of 6 Chinese, 5 in civilian clothes and one wearing semi-officers' dark green uniform with a hat bearing a crest of 2 crossed flags, one Japanese and the other of the Reformed Government.
This "officer" was in possession of a duplicate receipt book while the civilian members, all wearing arm bands were in possession of Reformed Government flags.
By keeping the party under observation it was observed that they were going from shop to shop selling their flags and if a sale was made the "officer" issued a receipt from his book.
Enquiries in several shops previously visiting by the party it was learned that although no pressure was made known regarding the purchase of a flag, the occupants of the places visited were "strongly advised" to buy a flag but if they could produce a Japanese or a Reformed Government flag no request to buy another

销售维新政府旗帜。
1939 年 3 月 27 日上午 11 时 10 分，督察 Sharrock 向虹口巡捕房报告称，他观察到一群身穿制服的市政府警察局成员和中国平民在世纪大道（Century Road）向居民处置维新政府旗帜。
经副督察 375 号和侦探 Muir 调查，锁定了一伙 6 名中国人，其中 5 人穿便衣，一人身穿半军官式的深绿色制服，头戴饰有交叉双旗徽章的帽子，一面为日本旗，另一面为维新政府旗。
这名“军官”持有一本复写收据簿，而便衣成员均佩戴臂章，持有维新政府旗帜。
通过对该伙人进行监视观察，发现他们逐店销售旗帜，若达成交易，“军官”便从其簿中开具收据。
在该伙人此前走访过的几家店铺中进行查询后获悉，虽然在购买旗帜方面未施加明显压力，但被访处所的住户受到“强烈建议”购买旗帜，但如果能出示日本或维新政府旗帜，则不会要求其再购买

关于复兴东亚国旗公司（Room 520, China Merchants Stock Exchange Building, Kiukiang Road (Tel.95497)）致各巡捕房及警察总局的通函，主题是促进国际租界内的国旗销售并请求警方协助开展此项运动，本人谨报告如下：该公司共同发起人周鸿宾于 1941 年 12 月 30 日上午 10 时在特别课总部接受问询，从中查明了以下细节：

复兴东亚国旗公司由周鸿宾和一位名叫叶芝庭的人发起，于 1941 年 12 月 25 日在日本军方特务机关的许可下正式成立。该公司受托在日本占领区推广国旗销售，旨在宣传“和平运动”的真谛。根据日本军方特务机关的规定，每面旗帜售价为日元 1.20 元或 5.00 元。这些旗帜以每面 4.50 元的价格从已停止运作的复兴公司购入。

East-Asia National Flag Company,
December 29, 1941.

Gordon Road Police Station,
Shanghai Municipal Council.

Dear Sirs,

Since the stationing of the Japanese Army and Naval
Forces in the International Settlement on 8-12-41 for the
maintenance of peace and order, we realize the residents and
various shops do not take much notice of peace and therefore
have requested the Japanese Authorities to issue us with a
certificate authorizing of the sale of the "Peace and Anti-
Communism Flags" to all people so as to make them understand
the importance of peace.

We are now detailing our salesmen to advise the
public to buy the flags within the Jurisdiction of the International
Settlement.

We enclose herewith a specimen of an identification
card for each of our staff, please place it on your record for
future reference.

Our Head Office is situated at 14 Zung Foh Li,
Fong Sung Road, Chapel and our temporary sales office is at
House 11, Lane Canton Road, telephone No. 93948.

Signed :- Tseu Hoong Bing,- representative
East-Asia National Flag Company.

from East-Asia National Flag Company.

East-Asia National Flag Company,
December 29, 1941.

Gordon Road Police Station,
Shanghai Municipal Council.

Dear Sirs,

Since the stationing of the Japanese Army and Naval
Forces in the International Settlement on 8-12-41 for the
maintenance of peace and order, we realize the residents and
various shops do not take much notice of peace and therefore
have requested the Japanese Authorities to issue us with a
certificate authorizing of the sale of the "Peace and Anti-
Communism Flags" to all people so as to make them understand
the importance of peace.

We are now detailing our salesmen to advise the
public to buy the flags within the Jurisdiction of the International
Settlement.

We enclose herewith a specimen of an identification
card for each of our staff, please place it on your record for
future reference.

Our Head Office is situated at 14 Zung Foh Li,
Fong Sung Road, Chapei and our temporary sales office is at
House 11, Lane Canton Road, telephone No. 93948.

Signed :- Tseu Hoong Bing,- representative
East-Asia National Flag Company.

My name is Dong Pah-tsoo, age 26, a native of
Pootung, residing at No.183 Yien Ching Li (延慶里),
corner of Rue Auguste Boppe and Rue Baron Gros , French
Concession, and I am a tailor in the employ of the Shing Hwa
Company (興華洋行), 139 Hsiang San Road, Chapei.
Ten days ago, through the introduction of my friend
Chang Ching-kwen (張金坤), who is now unemployed at
Pootung, I joined the "Shanghai Central-China National Flag
Sales Promotion Society (上海華中國旗勸銷社 ) as a
salesman. This society is located at No.28 Yung Chi Li (永
吉里), Weihaiwei Road, which is also the residence of Sung
Kuh-ziang (沈克翔), Chief of the society.
At about 10 a.m. January 1, I left my home and
called at the society, where Sung Kuh-ziang gave me an
identification card together with twenty-five national flags,
and instructed me to sell the flags at the prices of $4 and
$6 each for No.4 and No.5 sizes respectively. A commission
of $2 on No.4 size flag and $1.15 on No.5 size would be given
to me for each flag sold.
I then left the society with the flags and
proceeded along Weihaiwei Road in a westerly direction and via
Seymour Road, to Gordon Road, selling the flags throughout the
journey. At about 2 p.m. I arrived at Zung Ka Hong (東家巷,
where I met two salesmen of the Poh Shing East Asia National
Flag Company, located in Room 520, 6th floor, China Merchants
Stock Exchange Building, Kiukiang Road (Tel.95497). They
took me to Room No.11 of the Yung Loh Hotel (永樂旅館),

Translation of a letter

Branch

Dated: January 1, 1942.

To the Special Branch,
S.M.P.

According to reports by our Inspectors, one
Dong Pah Tsoo (唐伯初), in possession of an
indentification card of the Shanghai Central-China
National Flag Sales Promotion Society (上海華中
國旗推銷社), sold flags in the vicinity of
Weihaiwei, Sinza, Gordon Roads and Zung Ka Hong, at
prices other than those fixed by this company. He
demanded $6 for a No.5 size flag and $4 for a No.4
size flag.

Furthermore, his statement that his
organization is "registered" with the Central
Propaganda Department cannot be confirmed.

We are therefore sending Dong Pah-tsoo to
you so that he can be dealt with for his illegal
activity.

(Sealed) Chow Hung-ping (周鴻賓),
representative of the Foh
Shing East Asia National
Flag Co. (復興東亞國旗公司)

My name is Sung Kuh-ziang, a e 25, a native of
Shanghai, residing at House 28, Yung Chi Li ( 永 吉 里 ),
Weihaiwei Road. I was unemployed following the outbreak
of the Sino-Japanese hostilities until September, 1941
when my friend Zau Hwa-chien ( 趙 華 劍 ) established
a "Shanghai Central-China National Flag Sales Promotion
Society" ( 上海華中國旗勸銷社 ) at 220 Yue Yuen Road
( 豫 園 路 ), Nantao. Since then I have been employed
by the society to take charge of its affairs. All the
flags - No.4 and No.5 sizes - are made by me and are sold
at a price of $4 each for No.4 size (cost price $2.50)
and $6 each for No.5 size (cost price $4). The profits,
after deducting a commission of $0.80 and $1.10 for the
salesman on each No.4 or No.5 size flag sold, and other
expenses of the society, are taken by Mr. Zau. This
society has at present only six salesmen, namely Chang
Dah-mao ( 張 大 毛 ), Doo Han-ming ( 杜 漢 明 ), Doo Siao-
ziang ( 杜 小 祥 ), Chang Liang-ming ( 張 良 明 ), Yeo
Mo-dzien ( 奚 木 泉 ), and Dong Fah-tsoo ( 唐 伯 初 ).
Casual hands are to be temporarily employed when required.

As this society supports the Peace Movement and New
Order of East Asia, the staff employees are selling the
national flags without using forcible means.

N.B. (1) Zau Hwa-chien is at present engaged in the
Nanking Government, and during his absence,
I took charge of the affairs of the society,
Mr. Zau resides at House 13, Woo Ping Hong
( 和 平 巷 ) Foh Shing Road ( 復 興 路 ), Nanking.

敬启者：

随函附上签发给我方员工的身份证样本一份，这些员工正在国际租界内从事和平及反共国旗的销售工作。

我们进行国旗销售的意图，是促使国际租界的店主和居民认识到和平运动的真正理念，因为自1941年12月8日日军占领国际租界以来，他们对这一理念或多或少感到陌生。

期待贵方的友好合作。

代表：周鸿平（Chow Hung Ping），

Despatch No. 105 Character "Tong" from Asia Rehabilitation
National Flags Company, addressed to Pootoo Road Police Station.
dated December 19th, 1941.

Pootoo Road Police Station.

This is to inform you that since December 8th,
1941, the Military and Navy Forces of the Greater Japan
have entered the International Settlement to maintain
order and peace therein. Owing to the shop keepers and
dwellers pay much concern to the peace movement policy, we
(the Company) petitioned to the Special Service Authorities
of Greater Japan at Shanghai and with their approval by
issuing a testimonial to sell the National Flags of "Peace,
Anti-Communist & Construction of Nation" in order to make the
people to understand the true idea of Peace Movement. Now,
we have sent employees to the Settlement to pursuade the
people to buy the flags.

Apart from the above, we submit this letter
with a sample of our employee's identification card for
your information and to asking you to render any assistance
to us in case if wanted.

N.B. The Office of our Company is situating at
No. 14 Zung Foh Li Alleyway, off Foh Sung Road,
Chapei.
Settlement temporary sales office is at No.
11, Lane 440, Canton Road. Tel. No. 93948.

Enclosed one sample of employee's
identification card.

Representative: Chow Hung Ping.

发自亚洲复兴国旗公司，致普陀路捕房的第105号“通”字公函，
日期：1941年12月19日。

普陀路捕房。

特此通知，自1941年12月8日起，大日本帝国海陆军进入国际租界以维持其中的秩序与和平。鉴于店主和居民对和平运动政策颇为关注，我们（本公司）向驻上海大日本帝国特别服务当局请愿，并获得批准，颁发证明书允许销售“和平、反共及建国”国旗，以使民众理解和平运动的真正理念。现在，我们已派遣员工进入租界，劝说民众购买国旗。

除上述事项外，随函附上我方员工身份证样本一份，供贵处知悉，并请在需要时向我们提供协助。

注：本公司办公室位于闸北复松路旁众福里14号。
租界临时销售处位于广东路440弄11号。电话：93948。
